author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A magazine checked out from the Concord Public Library in September 1894 has returned after 48,220 days, or more than 132 years. John Hanson, a Barrington resident who previously lived in Boscawen, brought back the September 1894 issue of “The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine.”

Library staff verified the date, issue and institutional bookplate. At the old rate of 25 cents a day, the overdue charge would have reached $12,055. Hanson avoided that theoretical bill because the library had frozen overdue fines for a year, a policy intended to reduce barriers to returning materials and using library services.

The periodical will not go back into ordinary circulation. Instead, the library plans to display it in the Concord Room, where local-history materials are kept. The return turns an unusually long loan into a tangible link with the city’s nineteenth-century readers while also giving the library’s fine-free period a memorable result. The unusual return also drew statewide attention.
dek: A September 1894 periodical came home after 48,220 days, with its notional $12,055 fine erased by a fine freeze.
headline: 132-year-overdue magazine returns to Concord Public Library
